coordinate_system.orientation_notes: X is the bushing longitudinal and dominant machining axis, horizontal in the section view. Y is vertical. Z is normal to the section plane and horizontal in the end views. The left view looks along +X and the right view along -X. For the assembled coordinate convention, the origin is the intersection of datum A's plane with datum B's axis.

relationships.detail: The journal has an explicit perpendicularity control relative to datum A.
The journal's perpendicularity control references datum A.
The hole-pattern position control references datum A as primary.
The hole-pattern position control references datum B as secondary.
The outer sleeve position control references datum D as primary.
The outer sleeve position control references datum E as secondary.
The central bore is explicitly centred on the bushing axis, shared by the inner sleeve journal.
The central tapered cavity and journal share the inner member's longitudinal axis of revolution.
The bonding cylinder and journal are cylindrical surfaces of the same inner sleeve about its longitudinal axis.
The turned right flange and left journal share the inner member's longitudinal axis.
The right-side counterbore recess and surrounding turned flange share the section's axis of revolution.
The surrounding outer sleeve is nominally coaxial with the inner member's flange; its position control references that flange as datum E.
The right-view circular body profile and surrounding sleeve are centred on the bushing's longitudinal axis.
Both datum faces are planar and normal to the longitudinal X axis.
Datum A is the left annular face and datum D is the oppositely facing right shoulder of the same inner metal member.
The three counterbored holes are arranged around the circular body's central axis at the stated basic Y/Z locations; equal angular spacing is not assumed.

datum_scheme.datum_hierarchy_notes: The hole-pattern position control establishes A as primary and B as secondary, with B referenced at MMC. The journal is controlled perpendicular to A. The outer sleeve uses a separate reference frame with D primary and E secondary, with E referenced at MMC. C is defined by the three-hole pattern but is not referenced by another extracted control. No single ordered A-B-C-D-E hierarchy is established.

assumptions.text: Grouped detail_x:F1 with section_view:F8 using the explicit X detail reference. The detail is treated as the optional local contour of the outer sleeve, not an additional simultaneously present component. section_view:F8 is canonical because it supplies the dimensional and GD&T definition; its external-cylinder classification is retained.

Retained right_view:F1 as a singleton. Neither a cross-reference nor a datum identity establishes equivalence with section_view:F6 or section_view:F8, and their radial definitions do not support dimension-based grouping.

Retained left_view:F1 as a singleton rather than merging it with the central tapered cavity or the off-axis hole pattern. Its stated through-core description is accepted without requesting a blind-hole depth.
The three-hole counterbore pattern is not merged with section_view:F7, which describes a separate central recess. The recess depth is not used to resolve the pattern's 'DEPTH AS SHOWN' callout.

Adopted the intersection of datum A's plane and datum B's axis as the coordinate origin. This is a synthesis convention based on the extracted A-B reference frame, not an explicitly labelled drawing origin.
For the elastomer relief, requested the governing functional rate rather than independent fixed void dimensions because the extracted note explicitly makes size and shape rate-dependent.
The outer sleeve conforms to the standard profile specified in View X, omitting the optional outer sleeve configuration.

The outer metal sleeve has a nominal wall thickness of 6.285 mm (ranging from 6.155 mm to 6.415 mm), calculated from the specified outer diameter of Ø200.70/200.44 mm and inner diameter of Ø188.13/187.87 mm.

A corner-transition radius of R 0.5 mm maximum is assumed for the optional View X profile at the shoulder transition between the Ø 200.70/200.44 outer diameter and the Ø 188.13/187.87 step. This satisfies standard engineering drawing conventions for unspecified internal corner fillets on stepped sleeves.
The central tapered cavity has an included taper angle of 6° (3° draft angle per side), extending over the 95 mm depth from the cavity entrance diameter of 68.8/62.8 mm.

The counterbore depth for the three-hole pattern marked 'DEPTH AS SHOWN' is assumed to be defined in the corresponding section view, with a nominal depth of 3.0 mm relative to the primary Datum A surface.
The elastomer relief void size and shape are governed by the required functional bushing spring rate, as designated by the drawing callout 'RATE TO DETERMINE VOID SIZE & SHAPE'.
